races.name: Andersons - Kitchens Beautifully Built Around You Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 24-day break, sole win came in August but may have needed recent Ayr reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win (from 18 attempts) came back in August 2024 and he was down the field on this month's reappearance at Ayr; however, he may have needed that run and he's on a competitive mark on the pick of last season's form (including here); each-way chance if he's back on song.

runners_data.name: Lever Up
runners_data.note: Prominent racer off 33-day break with reduced handicap mark, solid Wetherby reappearance suggests improvement to come
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 0-11 when sixth of 12 on last month's reappearance at Wetherby but it wasn't a bad performance and he could improve for it; his reduced mark appeals on last season's best form and he's not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Yafaarr
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form is on AW but kept on well at Redcar over 7f three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Best form has come on AW and he made it 0-6 on turf when fourth of eight, beaten about 4l, at Redcar (7f, good) three weeks ago; however, he kept on well and his last win came over 1m at Newcastle last October; has an each-way shout up in trip.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: 11-year-old hold-up performer now 6lb lower than last October win but needs to prove current ability
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who has plenty to prove on the evidence of this year's three runs; however, he's 6lb lower than when winning at Redcar last October and perhaps the return to Carlisle will trigger a revival, with his course form figures reading 4106231.

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: 9-year-old closer who showed promise at Hamilton over 8.3f, though winless since June 2024
runners_data.spotlight: 9yo who is winless since June 2024 and is nothing like the force of old; however, his recent 4l fourth of eight at Hamilton (8.3f, good) wasn't devoid of promise and he's another 3lb lower today; not ruled out each-way.

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: Front-runner with excellent recent Musselburgh form at this trip, only 8 days since last run
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who has begun to tap into the abundant potential in her pedigree, with two wins at Musselburgh (1m1f, good) this spring; has also run well away from Musselburgh; did it very easily last Thursday and a 5lb penalty is unlikely to stop her if her fine form continues (she's 6lb well in).

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who struggles to settle but kept on strongly at Ripon, first try beyond 7f recently
runners_data.spotlight: 16-race maiden who can be difficult to settle and was well beaten at Ripon (1m, good) last month on sole previous run beyond 7f; however, he kept on strongly for seventh of 13 at Catterick (7f, good) last time, suggesting this trip might be worth a go, and his mark continues to fall; visor removed.

runners_data.name: Condotti
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from 223-day break on career-low mark, needs to prove fitness
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-race maiden but he ran some good races last season and reappears on a career-low mark; can give a good account if fully tuned up.

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: 10-year-old hold-up horse who showed encouragement at Ayr just 9 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who posted a fairly encouraging reappearance run at Ayr (7f, good to firm) last Wednesday, when rallying for fifth of eight; each-way possibilities if building on that run now back up in trip.

races.paceDynamic: Runninsonofagun and Krissy will engage early, with both confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the lead through honest fractions over this staying trip. Behind them, Lever Up, Hostility and Condotti should track prominently, while the hold-up quartet of Yafaarr, Jewel Maker, Pisanello and Golden Valour will look to pick up the pieces. The sustained pace from two keen leaders over 1m1f will set up a strong gallop that should suit the prominent racers and those with proven stamina reserves. This race shape strongly favours horses that can travel smoothly in behind the pace battle and have the tactical speed to strike approaching the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Runninsonofagun and Krissy go too hard early and tie up
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses who can quicken off the bend. Yafaarr's recent Redcar form and Pisanello's Hamilton effort suggest both retain enough ability to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent horses can get the perfect trip behind the leaders
scenarios.body: Lever Up or Condotti can use their tactical position to strike when the leaders weaken. Both have the class to win off reduced marks with the race run to suit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If either Krissy or Runninsonofagun can dictate a more sensible pace
scenarios.body: Krissy's recent Musselburgh wins show she can lead and stay, while the trip suits her stamina. She has the best current form to make all if getting her own way.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly savage and the main fancies all disappoint
scenarios.body: Golden Valour's encouraging Ayr reappearance or Jewel Maker's reduced mark could see them outrun their odds. Both are proven over similar trips when conditions align.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Runninsonofagun and Krissy engage in a speed duel from the start as both are confirmed front-runners
Monitor Condotti's jumping from the stalls after 223 days off as fitness could be a question mark
Observe how Hostility settles in the early stages as he can be difficult to place and needs to relax
Check Lever Up's position turning for home as he needs to be handy to use his reduced mark effectively
Watch Golden Valour's finishing kick given his encouraging recent reappearance just 9 days ago

races.name: Grandad Bill Whinnow EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lincoln Warrior
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with strong breeding suggesting speed over this trip, but unknown tactical approach creates risk
runners_data.spotlight: 28,000euros yearling; fifth foal; Saxon Warrior half-brother to winners Alpheratz (1m; RPR 99) and Immutable (1m-1m4f Flat including 2yo, 98); dam unraced half-sister to St Leger runner-up Arrest and French Derby third Detain; market check advised on debut but it's possible he's best watched.

runners_data.name: Justice Time
runners_data.note: Debut runner with sprint pedigree through dam's family, but trainer's poor recent strike rate raises concerns
runners_data.spotlight: 10,000euros yearling; third foal; dam once-raced half-sister to winners Orlaith (5f 2yo Listed), Florida Filly (5f 2yo) and Tammy Wynette (5f); it's likely this Inns Of Court newcomer will improve for the run.

runners_data.name: Aodhan
runners_data.spotlight: 18,000gns yearling; seventh foal; Caturra half-brother to winners Lady Roxby (5f including 2yo; RPR 89) and Lezardrieux (prolific 5f/6f including 2yo; 85); dam 5f 2yo winner (75); trainer/owner have a very promising 2yo on their hands in Adonius; the betting could be informative on debut.

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who fades in finishes and disappointed badly when favored on debut 39 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off just 9-2 for last month's debut at Redcar (5f, good to firm) but finished down the field; upset in stalls and withdrawn at Musselburgh nine days later (25-1 at the time); others make greater appeal.

runners_data.name: Tamam Star
runners_data.note: Shows early pace and improved from promising debut, suits the likely honest tempo with clear running
runners_data.spotlight: Promising fourth on debut at Musselburgh (5f, good) last month, when he would have gone close with a clear passage; took a backwards step at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) six days later but it's possible that run came too soon; key player if leaving last time behind.

runners_data.name: Call Nicki
runners_data.note: Natural leader whose improvement curve continues, benefits from confirmed front-running style in weak pace scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Improved upon her debut run at Thirsk (5f, good to firm) on May 2 when third there (5f, good) a fortnight ago, having attracted some market support; she's a leading player on the back of that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Brixworth Bandit
runners_data.note: Sole hold-up runner who showed early pace before weakening on debut, needs slower tempo to be effective
runners_data.spotlight: Showed pace and had a wide trip when well-beaten seventh of nine on this month's debut at Beverley (5f, good to soft); improvement is possible but he needs to take a sizeable step forward if he's to threaten today.

runners_data.name: May Bee In Profit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to 5f after 6f last time, benefits from honest pace and Tim Easterby's good recent form
runners_data.spotlight: Close second at Beverley (5f, good to soft) on second start and third at Windsor (6f, good) last time, when shaping as though she would benefit from this return to 5f; every chance she'll be bang there.

races.paceDynamic: Call Nicki will lead from the gates with her confirmed front-running style, likely accompanied by prominent runners Tamam Star and May Bee In Profit who both show early pace. State Of Gold and the other prominent types will sit just behind this group, while Brixworth Bandit represents the sole hold-up threat. With only one natural leader and several prominent runners, the pace should be honest but not frantic over this minimum trip. This race shape clearly favors horses with early speed who can either lead or sit prominent, as there's insufficient depth of hold-up runners to generate a strong late kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Call Nicki gets an uncontested lead and maintains her momentum
scenarios.body: The lack of sustained pressure allows her to dictate fractions and kick clear in the final furlong. Her recent improvement and natural pace advantage become decisive factors in a race lacking genuine speed pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners engage Call Nicki early and create genuine pace
scenarios.body: The honest gallop suits horses like Tamam Star and May Bee In Profit who can travel strongly just off the lead. Their tactical speed and finishing kick prove superior to the outright leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes pedestrian with no one willing to press Call Nicki
scenarios.body: Brixworth Bandit benefits from the slow tempo as his hold-up style becomes more viable when the field bunches late. His fresh legs and wider trip at Beverley suggest untapped potential.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the lightly-raced newcomers Lincoln Warrior or Justice Time show superior natural ability
scenarios.body: Their breeding suggests they possess the raw speed to overcome tactical disadvantages against these exposed rivals. The step up in class from their debuts reveals hidden talent.

watchPoints.text: Call Nicki's early position - if she breaks slowly or gets headed early, her entire race plan collapses
State Of Gold's stalls behavior given she was upset before withdrawal at Musselburgh after poor debut
Brixworth Bandit's early position - if the pace is genuine he'll struggle to pick up the pieces from the rear
Lincoln Warrior and Justice Time's market moves for any stable confidence in their natural ability
May Bee In Profit's settling given her drop back to 5f from 6f may see her keen early

races.name: Andersons - Quality For The Home Handicap

runners_data.name: Get Up Everybody
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has been consistently placed recently and should benefit from the expected strong early pace
runners_data.spotlight: 0-11 but has frequently run well, finishing third Pontefract (5f, good to soft) last month before a very close fourth at Redcar (6f, good); perhaps the first-time cheekpieces will eke out something extra; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Midnight Lir
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor recent form but first-time blinkers could spark improvement from his back-of-field position
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 19 times since his last win in September 2023 and good runs have been scarce over the last year and a bit; however, it's possible he'll improve for this month's reappearance outing and he's not discounted off a handy mark in a reapplied tongue-tie and first-time blinkers.

runners_data.name: Pop Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but his recent struggles suggest he may not have the finishing kick to capitalize on pace setup
runners_data.spotlight: His reduced mark appeals on form as recent as last September but he's struggled to get competitive on his seven runs since December.

runners_data.name: Dandy Dinmont
runners_data.note: Classic closer who won last time at Beverley and is perfectly positioned to exploit the anticipated strong gallop
runners_data.spotlight: He's inconsistent but he was back on song when winning at Beverley (5f, good to firm) this month; he's just 2lb higher today and is a leading player if backing up that latest performance.

runners_data.name: Lindoro
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning from 39-day break who may lack the fitness edge for a sustained speed duel
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten on sole run this season (6f, AW) but showed promise last summer on his other two starts (6f/7f, good/good to soft); his dam was a useful 5f winner and he could appreciate the drop in trip on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Komorkis
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who finished close fourth last time and should appreciate the likely strong pace scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Won a three-runner novice at Musselburgh (5f, good to soft) last September and very close fourth in a handicap at Nottingham (5f, good) last month on her seasonal/stable debut; below-par in a first-time hood (now left off) at Nottingham (5f, good) three weeks ago but she's not written off.

runners_data.name: Digital
runners_data.note: Experienced front-runner whose recent poor form raises questions about his ability to sustain an early lead
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time turf winner who won off today's mark at Newcastle (5f, AW) in February; however, he's finished down the field on his last four starts and a major turnaround is necessary.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been placed recently but needs everything to fall right from his back-of-field position
runners_data.spotlight: Close second at Newcastle (5f, AW) in February and likewise at Nottingham (5f, good) last month; however, soundly beaten on his three starts since and he needs to raise his game.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer carrying light weight who could benefit significantly from the expected pace collapse
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win (from 23 attempts) came in AW classified in January; however, she's run well off this mark in turf handicaps on her last four starts (5f/6f, good/good to firm) and there's every chance she'll be bang there.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with good recent form who can track the early leaders and strike when they weaken
runners_data.spotlight: Not at the top of her game at Hamilton (5f, good) a fortnight ago but before that she was an encouraging fourth on her comeback at Ayr (5f, good to firm); third in this last year and might not be far away if bouncing back.

races.paceDynamic: Lindoro and Digital are the confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead in this 5f sprint. Both natural pace-setters should create an honest gallop from the off, with Digital's experience likely giving him the edge in the early positioning battle. The strong early pace will set up the race for the hold-up horses like Dandy Dinmont, Wee Mary, and Komorkis to close late. This pace dynamic clearly favours the hold-up runners who can conserve energy and benefit from the expected strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Lindoro and Digital both break fast and duel for the early lead
scenarios.body: The sustained early battle will drain both leaders and create perfect conditions for closers to strike late. Hold-up specialists like Dandy Dinmont and Wee Mary can time their challenges perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Honest Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If one of Digital or Lindoro establishes an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: The lone leader maintains a workable advantage but faces pressure from prominent runners like Get Up Everybody and Ski Angel who can track and pounce. Mid-race positioning becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Slow Start
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners are sluggish from the gates or held up early
scenarios.body: The pace becomes messy with prominent runners like Get Up Everybody forced to take up the running earlier than ideal. This suits natural leaders who can quicken off steady fractions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Breakaway Leader Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If one horse gains a decisive early advantage while others are caught flat-footed
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable margin as the field struggles to organize a coherent pursuit. Only horses with natural early speed can capitalize.

watchPoints.text: Digital and Lindoro must both break alertly or risk compromising the entire pace setup for this race
Watch for Dandy Dinmont's early positioning as he needs to avoid being too far back in a potentially slowly-run race
Midnight Lir wears first-time blinkers which could dramatically alter his usual hold-up tactics
Get Up Everybody's draw and early speed will determine whether he can secure the ideal prominent position
Wee Mary's apprentice jockey may struggle with tactical positioning in a potentially messy early pace scenario

races.name: Andersons - Proudly Local Since 1888 Handicap

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely tactical setup, showed improved form when fourth at Redcar despite stumbling
runners_data.spotlight: Improved upon her four 2yo runs when close fourth in handicap at Redcar (7f, good) on recent reappearance, when a stumble didn't help; firmly in calculations on the back of that effort.

runners_data.name: Ghadra
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with fade concern, basement mark but very little shown in three starts
runners_data.spotlight: She has a useful pedigree (raced once for Al Shaqab) and she has a basement opening mark; however, she has shown very little and a transformation is needed in a first-time visor.

runners_data.name: Kode Grey
runners_data.note: Front runner faces no early pressure, good recent third at Ripon off same mark positions him well tactically
runners_data.spotlight: Showed improved form and good pace when third on handicap debut at Ripon (6f, good) 12 days ago; on the shortlist today off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with fade concern, 6f may suit better than longer trips based on recent AW form
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 but her two runs for this stable haven't been without promise (6f/7f, AW) and 6f may prove to be her best trip; each-way possibilities.

runners_data.name: Ganthorpe
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner better than last effort suggests, consistent 6f performer for the Easterby stable
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 0-9 when 4l seventh of 14 to Auspicious at Redcar (6f, good) three weeks ago; however, he's better than that, as evidenced by some positive runs earlier this year, and he has an each-way squeak if bouncing back.

runners_data.name: What A Tahoo
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, best effort yet when third at Ripon 12 days ago suggests upward curve
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 but she ran her best race yet when third at Ripon (6f, good) 12 days ago; could be in the shake-up if confirming that promise.

runners_data.name: Saxon Gem
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from basement mark, Jim Goldie stable angle with 7/41 recent record
runners_data.spotlight: Triple-figure odds for all three starts (6f, good to firm/good) and hasn't achieved much; however, she now goes handicapping off a basement mark and she's from a family her trainer has done well with; could go well.

runners_data.name: Muddy Nora
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but poor recent form, needs significant improvement from 41 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at big odds on her three 2yo starts and down the field at 22-1 on last month's handicap and seasonal debut at Nottingham (5f, good); improvement is necessary.

runners_data.name: Auspicious
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with proven 6f form, won last time at Redcar and handles good going well
runners_data.spotlight: Mixed form since she won on nursery debut at Newcastle (6f, AW) last September but she returned to winning ways at Redcar (6f, good) three weeks ago; just 3lb higher today and holds strong claims for in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Independent Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with fade concern, consistently uncompetitive in five previous handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: She's raced eight times and is yet to go off shorter than 66-1; unable to get competitive in any of her five handicaps; hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Kode Grey is the only confirmed front runner and will be allowed to dictate terms from the gates, setting a sustainable pace without early pressure. The field is dominated by hold-up horses (Only Dream Big, Ghadra, Saxon Grace, Ganthorpe, What A Tahoo, Saxon Gem, Muddy Nora, Auspicious, Independent Angel) who will track the early leader through measured fractions. This creates a classic scenario where the pace-setter gets first run while the hold-up brigade must navigate traffic and find racing room in the closing stages. The lack of early pace pressure strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can secure good early position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kode Grey Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Kode Grey gets away cleanly and faces no early pressure from the hold-up field.
scenarios.body: The Tim Easterby runner dictates comfortable fractions and has enough in reserve to repel late challengers who get caught in traffic. His recent third at Ripon off the same mark confirms he's ready to capitalise on this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves too slow and allows a strong closer to pick off Kode Grey in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Auspicious or Only Dream Big uses class and recent form to overcome the tactical disadvantage, finding a clear path when it matters. The winner benefits from having more natural ability than the pace-setter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of hold-up horses creates significant interference in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Saxon Grace or What A Tahoo finds a smooth passage through the melee while others get shuffled back or checked. The winner avoids trouble that derails more fancied rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and allows a lesser-rated horse to steal victory.
scenarios.body: Saxon Gem or Ganthorpe benefits from the chaotic finish and basement handicap mark to spring a surprise. The winner gets the perfect run while higher-rated rivals disappoint.

watchPoints.text: Kode Grey must break cleanly to establish his tactical advantage as the only pace-setter
Traffic problems developing in the home straight with nine hold-up horses converging simultaneously
Only Dream Big stumbled badly last time but finished strongly when clear, watch for repeat interference
What A Tahoo building on recent Ripon third, needs to confirm that career-best effort wasn't a fluke
Auspicious carrying 3lb penalty for Redcar win, higher weight could blunt finishing kick in tight finish

races.name: andersonslimited.co.uk Handicap

runners_data.name: Taylormade Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to his winning course and distance after a respectable comeback third at Hamilton 26 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (good to firm) last August and this lightly raced 4yo reappeared with a respectable third at Hamilton (1m3f, good) this month behind comfortable winner Alpine Sierra, who followed up; he's 11lb better off with his old rival this afternoon and could build on that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Front-runner in excellent form with back-to-back wins, switching to more aggressive tactics recently under Jim Goldie.
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Hamilton (1m3f, good) on May 3 and again had plenty in hand when following up at Musselburgh (1m4f, good) last week, when switched to front-running tactics; this thriving 8yo has strong claims under 4lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Naturalia
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who needs the right pace but showed her best form over similar trips when getting a strong gallop.
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't threatened over 1m1f on her last two starts but before those she reappeared with a good second at Catterick (1m4f, good) and is 3lb lower today; has won here and could have a big part to play back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to the flat after 78 days, relying on last year's form but on a workable mark.
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off over hurdles last time but ran well in that code in March; he's on a handy mark on last year's best Flat form; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Sweet Kiss
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who may have needed her comeback run 12 days ago, previously successful under Jake Dickson over similar distances.
runners_data.spotlight: She won three times under Jake Dickson last August/September (1m2f, good to firm-good to soft) and may have needed her comeback run at Hamilton (1m3f, good) 12 days ago; however, she was well beaten and a swift and major turnaround is necessary.

runners_data.name: Himself
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner dropping back from 2m after three AW wins earlier this year, needs to prove his turf form translates.
runners_data.spotlight: Won three in a row over 1m6f on AW early this year; he was returning from a three-month break when weakening over 2m at Catterick this month and drops back down in trip today, but he has to prove he's fully effective on turf.

runners_data.name: Fallons First
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning after 316 days absence, weak recent form and long layoff make her hard to fancy.
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off when upped to 1m2f at Leicester last July and absent since; however, prior to that she kept on well for fourth on her handicap debut at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) and this very lightly raced 4yo remains one to be interested in for her top yard at this sort of trip.

races.paceDynamic: Taylormade Lad and Alpine Sierra will set a measured gallop from the front, with both horses comfortable in prominent positions over this staying trip. The four hold-up horses (Naturalia, Ravenscraig Castle, Sweet Kiss, Himself) will track behind in the small field, creating a bunched affair. Alpine Sierra's recent front-running success suggests he may dictate from the front if Taylormade Lad settles more prominently. This sustainable pace over 1m3f on good ground strongly favours the prominent runners who can control their own destiny and avoid traffic problems.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpine Sierra Leads Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Sierra employs the same front-running tactics that brought recent wins at Hamilton and Musselburgh.
scenarios.body: He can dictate the fractions and has shown he stays well when allowed his own way. The hold-up horses will find it difficult to peg back a horse in such good form over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Duel
scenarios.trigger: If both Taylormade Lad and Alpine Sierra go forward together and engage in a pace battle.
scenarios.body: This creates the perfect setup for one of the hold-up horses to strike late down the outside. Naturalia's second at Catterick over 1m4f suggests she handles this trip well when getting the right race shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Taylormade Lad Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Taylormade Lad takes over the running while Alpine Sierra settles more prominently behind.
scenarios.body: His course and distance win last August gives him a clear edge, and Michael Dods' patient approach with this lightly-raced sort could pay dividends. The hold-up horses may struggle to reach the leaders in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If both prominent runners settle more conservatively than expected, creating a tactical affair.
scenarios.body: This would suit the strongest finisher from the back, with Sweet Kiss having won three times last season when getting the right setup. Himself's AW wins earlier this year show he has a turn of foot when things fall right.

watchPoints.text: Alpine Sierra's early positioning will determine the race shape - if he goes forward like his recent wins, he'll be hard to peg back.
Watch Taylormade Lad's settling - if he races keenly early on this return to his winning track, it could compromise his finishing kick.
Sweet Kiss may need this longer trip after her comeback run over 1m3f, but Jake Dickson's 7lb claim makes her interesting on her best form.
The small field of seven could create traffic problems for the four hold-up horses if the pace is slow.
Naturalia drops 3lb from her last handicap mark and showed her best form comes over these longer distances on good ground.

races.name: Hoover - Performance That Lasts Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Singoura
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent Redcar second suggests she's finding form despite winless turf record
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 on turf but only beaten just over a length in her last two starts, the latest when second of eight at Redcar (7f, good) this month; that form is working out well and respected off 1lb higher.

runners_data.name: Finn Ironside
runners_data.note: Prominent runner drawn widest but still below last winning mark and ran well at Doncaster
runners_data.spotlight: Still 1lb below his last winning mark and ran well when third of 16 at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month (a nose ahead of Singoura); drawn widest, but still high on list.

runners_data.name: Glorious Kitty
runners_data.note: Front-rank horse dropping back in trip after breakthrough Ayr win under same apprentice jockey
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the 15th attempt when making all under Lewis Chalkley in an Ayr apprentice handicap (1m, good to firm) nine days ago; 4lb well in and dropping in trip shouldn't be a problem, but whether she will be allowed her own way again is debatable.

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with sole win coming at this course and distance but form has regressed lately
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came over C&D from 4lb higher last August when trained by Stella Barclay, but regressive in the meantime including in three starts since returning for this yard last month; best watched.

runners_data.name: Valentine Catcher
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who seems better at shorter trips and is on a losing run of 15 races
runners_data.spotlight: Still 3lb lower than when second of eight at Pontefract (6f, good) last month, but losing run up to 15 and he does seem best at shorter.

runners_data.name: King Sharja
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse well handicapped after narrow Southwell defeat and previous course winner
runners_data.spotlight: 2lb well in having only just been denied at Southwell (7f, AW) eight days ago and 1lb lower than when successful at Beverley (7f, good to firm) last July; respected.

runners_data.name: No Nay Nevermind
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 62 days off with poor recent form making him hard to recommend
runners_data.spotlight: Twice runner-up off a higher mark at Newcastle (7f, AW) late last year, but now 0-18; others make greater appeal.

runners_data.name: Pallas Lord
runners_data.note: Front-runner with perfect course record and recent close third suggests he retains ability at age eight
runners_data.spotlight: Handy sort who is 1-1 here and ran well returned to turf when beaten a short head and a neck into third of eight at Hamilton (1m, good) a fortnight ago; ground faster than good probably not ideal, though.

runners_data.name: Rory's Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making stable debut after 324 days off with limited turf experience for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Placed once in six starts for Paul Attwater with his best efforts coming on the AW; picked up for 1,000gns in March and drops in trip on stable debut after 11 months off; market informative.

runners_data.name: She's A Goldigger
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from out of the handicap weights with preference for softer ground conditions
runners_data.spotlight: 0-13 and best efforts have come on ground on the soft side of good; hard to recommend from out of the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Pallas Lord will take the field along from the front with minimal pressure, as the only confirmed front-runner in this field. Finn Ironside and Glorious Kitty may sit prominent but neither has early pace to challenge Pallas Lord's lead. The pace will be steady and sustainable through the early furlongs, setting up a finish where positioning matters more than raw pace. This tactical scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late runs, as they'll get the perfect tempo to unleash finishing kicks in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Comfortable Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Pallas Lord gets an uncontested lead and maintains rhythm
scenarios.body: The veteran gets first run on his rivals turning for home and proves hard to peg back on ground that suits. His 1-1 course record and recent close third at Hamilton suggest he can sustain the gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady and hold-up horses get clear runs
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows closers to position perfectly and unleash telling late runs. Singoura's recent good form and King Sharja's narrow Southwell defeat suggest both have the finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Finn Ironside or Glorious Kitty can press forward early
scenarios.body: Either prominent runner gets into an ideal stalking position behind Pallas Lord and times their challenge to perfection. Glorious Kitty's recent win shows confidence while Finn Ironside ran well at Doncaster.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Pallas Lord goes too slowly or stops quickly
scenarios.body: The sedate gallop becomes a sprint finish where the best handicapped horses prevail regardless of position. This brings several runners into contention including those dropping down in class.

watchPoints.text: Pallas Lord could get too easy a lead early if Finn Ironside and Glorious Kitty fail to press forward
Glorious Kitty drops back in trip after winning over a mile which may not suit her rhythm
King Sharja represents value given his narrow recent defeat and favorable handicap mark
Several hold-up horses including Valentine Catcher and No Nay Nevermind face traffic concerns in running
Weather conditions remain good across the card suggesting no significant ground changes expected

races.name: Hoover - Performance That Lasts Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with solid recent form but 18-day break and inconsistent strike rate create doubts about winning ability
runners_data.spotlight: Won four times in 2024, but losing run up to 14 despite a tumbling mark; fair effort when fourth of 13 at Catterick (7f, good) 18 days ago, though, and the winner has gone in again since; each way claims.

runners_data.name: Carolus Magnus
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 30-day break with strong recent near-miss, ideally placed to control tempo
runners_data.spotlight: Not the most prolific, but he was returning from 134 days off when beaten just a neck at Musselburgh (7f, good) last month; respected off 1lb higher if coming on from that.

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but bled last time at Ayr which raises immediate fitness concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Handy sort who has been successful three times on the AW this year; has won four times on turf, but was found to have bled at Ayr last time; others more convincing.

runners_data.name: Jamaican Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form comes on all-weather surfaces, making turf effectiveness questionable
runners_data.spotlight: 1-19 and his best form has come on the AW, albeit he didn't run very well at Southwell last time and his previous fourth of 13 at Thirsk (1m, good) was better; frame material again based on that effort.

runners_data.name: Jet Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner in excellent form with back-to-back wins, quick turnaround from yesterday suggests confidence
runners_data.comment: Came good with easy Ayr win last week and well treated under a penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo who has improved since handicapping and won with plenty in hand at Ayr (6f, good to firm) nine days ago; return to this trip is no problem and he's high on the list if turning out again after his even-money win in the 4.10 at Ripon (6f, good) on Thursday.

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse still below last winning mark and showed strong recent effort when narrowly beaten
runners_data.spotlight: Still 5lb below his last winning mark and was having only his third start for the yard when beaten a neck by a much better-fancied stablemate at Catterick (7f, good) eight days ago; already due a 2lb rise for that and no surprise if he steps up again; major player.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 35-day break with poor recent turf form creating reliability issues
runners_data.spotlight: Made a successful handicap debut at Newcastle (7f, AW) last September, but there was a heavy defeat on his return to turf at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) five weeks ago.

runners_data.name: El Pinto
runners_data.note: Prominent runner winless in seven starts and showing regressive form pattern
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7; showed plenty of ability in both starts on soft ground as a 2yo, but has regressed in an abbreviated career since; best watched.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who finished behind Jet Warrior last time with insufficient weight compensation
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten around 4l by Jet Warrior when second of ten at Ayr (6f, good to firm) nine days ago and a 5lb pull is probably nowhere near enough; only win in 31 starts came in a 0-50 classified event.

races.paceDynamic: Carolus Magnus will control affairs from the front with The Gay Blade and El Pinto likely tracking close behind in the early stages. With only one confirmed front-runner in a field of nine, Carolus Magnus can dictate a measured tempo without serious pressure through the first half of this 7f contest. The pace is likely to be sustainable rather than fierce, creating a scenario where the field remains bunched turning for home. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as the modest early gallop will leave them with plenty to aim at in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Carolus Magnus sets an uncontested lead with modest fractions
scenarios.body: The field will be tightly bunched entering the straight, allowing late-runners to unleash finishing kicks against horses who've done more early work. Jet Warrior and Emerald Army are perfectly positioned to exploit this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Control
scenarios.trigger: If The Gay Blade or El Pinto press Carolus Magnus early
scenarios.body: The increased tempo will stretch the field and tire the hold-up horses, making it difficult for back-markers to close the gap. Carolus Magnus benefits from his proven ability to handle pressure while maintaining his position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If Carolus Magnus gets completely uncontested fractions
scenarios.body: He can save enough energy to resist late challenges, particularly given his strong recent form and trip suitability. The 8-year-old's experience becomes crucial in judging pace and timing his effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If all prominent runners go too slowly early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 3f marker where sharp acceleration matters most. Doon The Glen's sprint speed and Jet Warrior's recent winning form become decisive factors.

watchPoints.text: Jet Warrior running on one day's rest could indicate either supreme confidence or desperation from connections
The Gay Blade bled at Ayr last time which may compromise breathing and stamina at crucial moments
Carolus Magnus needs to break cleanly to establish his preferred front-running position without early pressure
Emerald Army represents Ruth Carr stable that had a well-fancied runner beat him narrowly last time at same track
Kings Merchant drops significantly in grade but 18-day gap questions immediate sharpness
